unexpected_issue_found_and_fixed.symptom: After restarting, the HUD took ~40s to appear (previously assumed hung, was actually just slow) and, more importantly, jarvis_app_v2.py launched via venv\Scripts\pythonw.exe turned out to relaunch itself as a CHILD process under a completely different interpreter -- C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python312\pythonw.exe (a system-wide Python install, not the project venv) -- and that child, not the parent, is the one that actually owns the HUD window and runs the live app.
unexpected_issue_found_and_fixed.root_cause_not_fully_identified: Traced this extensively (instrumented subprocess.Popen, checked sys._base_executable, grepped every jarvis_*.py file for Popen/pythonw/win32 process APIs) without finding the exact call site -- it does not go through subprocess.Popen, so it's likely a lower-level Windows API call or a multiprocessing-adjacent mechanism inside one of the many third-party packages. This predates today's session and is not something introduced by this migration.
unexpected_issue_found_and_fixed.practical_impact: Whichever interpreter actually ends up running the live app needs claude-agent-sdk/kokoro/etc. installed, not just whichever one you launch with. Confirmed system Python312 could import Jarvis's OTHER existing deps (vosk, pygame) via some sys.path sharing with the venv, but claude_agent_sdk specifically failed there via a pywin32 (pywintypes) DLL registration issue that does NOT reliably cross interpreters even when pure-Python packages do.
unexpected_issue_found_and_fixed.fix: Installed the same new package set (claude-agent-sdk, kokoro, sounddevice, soundfile, numpy, pynput, httpx, webrtcvad-wheels) directly into system Python312 via its own pip, so the import chain is self-contained there too regardless of which interpreter ends up live. Verified both interpreters can cleanly import claude_agent_sdk.ClaudeSDKClient and kokoro afterward.
unexpected_issue_found_and_fixed.still_recommended: Worth an eventual look (not urgent) at what specifically causes the relaunch, so Jarvis can be pinned to one interpreter and startup can be faster/more predictable -- flagging for a future session rather than continuing to chase it now that the practical fix is in place.

not_yet_externally_verified: Everything was verified by calling the same functions the wake-word path uses (ask_ai_common_v2, quick_handle_command_v2, install_v2's overrides) directly, plus confirming the HUD process now has every needed package.
